short_description: A phrase-by-phrase English translation of the Qur'an by Ali Quli Qara'i that mirrors the structure of the Arabic text while drawing on both Sunni and Shi'i classical exegesis to convey the most probable meaning of each passage.
detailed_description: Ali Quli Qara'i's 'The Qur'an with a Phrase-by-Phrase English Translation' is a distinctive translation designed to give English readers some of the benefits traditionally found in Persian and Urdu interlinear Qur'an editions. Rather than presenting a continuous translation, it uses a phrase-by-phrase 'mirror-paraphrasing' method, aligning English renderings with corresponding Arabic segments to make the grammatical and semantic structure of the original text more transparent.

The translation is not a standalone tafsir, but it is deeply informed by classical Qur'anic exegesis. Qara'i consulted major Sunni commentaries such as al-Tabari, al-Razi, al-Zamakhshari, and al-Suyuti, alongside important Shi'i works including al-Mizan of Allama Tabataba'i, Majma' al-Bayan of al-Tabrisi, and Tafsir al-Burhan. When multiple interpretations existed, he generally selected what he considered the strongest interpretation while occasionally noting significant alternatives in footnotes.

A defining feature of the work is its careful treatment of Qur'anic idioms. Expressions that remain intelligible when translated literally are preserved, while culturally specific or opaque idioms are paraphrased into natural English. In some cases, equivalent English idioms are employed to preserve rhetorical effect.

The translation also incorporates cross-references, extensive indexing, and special attention to exegetical traditions transmitted from the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt, whom the translator regards as an essential source for understanding Qur'anic meaning.

Compared with major tafsir works, this volume occupies a middle ground between a plain translation and a commentary. Unlike al-Mizan, which provides extensive philosophical, theological, linguistic, and intertextual analysis, Qara'i's work focuses on accurate translation and concise explanatory notes.

Unlike Tafsir Ibn Kathir, which relies heavily on hadith reports and early Sunni narrations to explain verses, Qara'i's translation seeks a broader exegetical synthesis, drawing from both Sunni and Shi'i traditions while giving particular weight to Shi'i hermeneutical sources.

The result is a translation that is more interpretive and academically informed than many literal English renderings, yet significantly more concise and accessible than comprehensive commentaries such as al-Mizan, Majma' al-Bayan, or Tafsir Ibn Kathir.
author: Ali Quli Qara'i
about_author: Ali Quli Qara'i is a contemporary Muslim scholar, translator, and researcher best known for translating classical Islamic texts into English. His work spans Qur'anic studies, hadith, philosophy, spirituality, and Shi'i scholarship. His reputation is built primarily on producing precise and readable English translations of important Islamic works while remaining attentive to the nuances of the original Arabic and Persian sources. In preparing his Qur'an translation, he consulted a wide range of Sunni and Shi'i exegetical authorities and paid particular attention to traditions attributed to the Prophet's family (Ahl al-Bayt). His approach is scholarly rather than polemical, aiming to make classical Islamic learning accessible to English-speaking audiences while preserving the interpretive depth of the tradition.
